main_text.l: Exoptata dies cum nos veneranda Geneva
Exoptata dies, cum nostra antiqua Nemausus
In viridi audiret plectra Daphnone Lyra.
Et cum trans Gardi triplicem nos Utica pontem
Quam mihi SANRAVI gratum coluisse Penates,
O utinam divina meas Hygiea Camenas
Quinque per hos menses miserè me exercuit ægrum
Frigidus heu stomachus, calidum jecur, atque cerebrum
Nunc mihi subducit vires, nunc reddit easdem:
Me DEUS horrisono servat in Oceano.
Illius arbitrio sto, surgo, cadoque, beatis
Donec tandem etiam me inserat ordinibus.

page.notes: The verse is set in italic with some words in roman capitals and small capitals; the signature line is in spaced capitals. Abbreviations such as "arte~", "pontem~", "eastdem~" and "atq;" are rendered as printed with the tilde or q-mark; the marks over "Quinq" and "Quinq;" are read as the abbreviation for -que. Some letter forms ("Quam", "Propositi") are uncertain in the scan. The date line "II.Febr.1627." is shown with the numeral form as printed. The ornament at the foot is not transcribed.
